transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Turner (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Jamie Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Synthesis IO), Carlos Mendez (Synthesis IO Sec), Ravi Patel (Synthesis IO ML), Maya (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
Synthesis IO is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployment: initial dev/test on Hosted, production on Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem). Key concerns: rate limits/quotas per-tenant, gateway/proxy pattern for multi-tenant edge, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter compatibility, observability hooks (per-route traces, token-level cost), and security (SOC2, KMS). Next steps: pricing, SDK examples, benchmark session.

Topics: integration, SDKs, gateway proxy, quotas, observability, security

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Alex from Redwood, Sam or Samira on the SE side, and Jamie for... jamie for solutions. Priya, Carlos, Ravi, Maya, you there?
[00:18] Priya (Synthesis IO): Yep, on the line. Thanks for setting this up — our team is in the middle of choosing between a hosted first approach or going straight to a private deployment. We wanted to run through integration patterns and what the onramp looks like.
[00:28] Samira (Redwood SE): Awesome. We'll try to keep this practical — walk through SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex hooks, gateway/proxy and the usual infra constraints. And we'll call out tradeoffs for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:38] Maya (PM): High level — our timeline is a Q3 production launch for the first product, but we want a pilot in May. Security is a blocker for some customers — need to understand KMS and audit logs.
[00:52] Carlos (Security): Yep. Plus data residency. We also have to confirm if token logs or raw prompt storage is retained anywhere in Redwood hosted.
[01:05] Alex: Great, we can cover that: hosted keeps only transient cache by default and we have controls for log retention, plus Dedicated/Private gives you customer-managed keys and audit logs. We'll send SOC2 docs after.
[01:18] Ravi (ML): Quick note — our stack uses LangChain for agents and LlamaIndex for retrieval pipelines. We need examples on how Redwood SDKs plug in, and how we do streaming responses with the agent loops.
[01:33] Samira: Totally. We have a LangChain adapter in our SDK, and we also have a LlamaIndex connector sample. I'll point you to a repo that contains a streaming example with prefix caching and KV cache management.
[01:48] Priya: When you say "adapter", is that a drop-in client or more of a transform layer? We want minimal changes to our orchestrator.
[02:00] Jamie: It's typically a client wrapper so you can swap the underlying model endpoint. For LangChain it looks like a provider class; for LlamaIndex it's a connector. There might be small call signature differences but it's usually a 10-30 line swap.
[02:14] Priya: Okay, good.
[02:20] [02:20] Speaker 1: mm-hmm.
[02:28] Alex: On the network side, if you go Private (VPC) you'll have a customer-controlled control plane and we support VPC peering and private links. For on-prem we have an air-gapped package but that's more of an enterprise setup.
[02:44] Carlos: For Dedicated, do you support bringing your own KMS or do we have to use Redwood's managed keys?
[02:52] Alex: With Dedicated you can optionally integrate with your KMS. With Private, the customer manages keys fully. On Hosted we offer envelope encryption and managed KMS by default but you can discuss a hybrid.
[03:05] Priya: Rate limits — can we do per-tenant quotas and burst policies? We need to throttle at the gateway level.
[03:16] Samira: Yes, per-route and per-API-key quotas are supported. We have soft and hard limits, and token-based billing so you can set quotas in tokens per minute and enforce spikes with burst windows. Also can route high priority traffic to Dedicated pool.
[03:32] Ravi: How about prefix/KV cache and batching — do you expose hooks to control cache TTLs?
[03:40] Samira: We expose config APIs to set cache TTL, max cached tokens, and batching windows. There's also automatic adaptive batching enabled by workload, but you can pin a policy per model or route.
[03:52] Maya: Observability — we need per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdown available in our telemetry. Can we ship traces to our tracing backend?
[04:02] Jamie: Yes, we support exporting traces to Jaeger/OTLP and sending metrics to Prometheus/Datadog. We also provide per-request cost metadata in logs and a token breakdown in the console and via the API.
[04:16] Carlos: Are audit logs S3-compatible and can they be retained under our retention policy?
[04:24] Alex: For Dedicated and Private, yes — audit logs can be pushed to customer S3 buckets, and retention policies are configurable. Hosted has an export feature and a retention window.
[04:35] [04:35] Priya: Ok. One more: gateway/proxy pattern — we run an internal API gateway. Do you recommend sidecar vs central gateway? We're worried about complexity and latency.
[04:47] Samira: If low-latency is critical, sidecar or local edge proxy helps reduce network hops. For multi-tenant central gateway patterns, you can use Redwood's ingress with per-tenant routing and encrypted headers. We usually see central gateway for teams that want single control plane and sidecar for teams with extreme latency constraints.
[05:05] Priya: What about connection pooling and persistent KV cache across pods?
[05:12] Jamie: The SDK supports pooling, and the runtime has sticky session options so KV cache can be warmed on particular instances. For very large scale we recommend Dedicated with reserved pools to keep warm caches and avoid cold starts.
[05:25] Ravi: Any constraints around model variants or fallback? We might want to failover to a smaller quantized model when latency spikes.
[05:33] Samira: Yes — routing policies let you specify preferred family, quantized fallback, and region fallback. You can set cost thresholds that trigger fallback automatically.
[05:46] Alex: Also want to call out quantization tradeoffs — 4-bit/8-bit quant gives big cost savings but you might see slight quality shifts. We can run evals against your prompt sets to quantify that.
[05:58] Maya: Can we run those evals before committing to Dedicated? We'd like an evidence-based decision.
[06:05] Alex: Absolutely — we'll run a pilot with your prompt sets and traffic shape. That's a standard step.
[06:12] [06:12] Carlos: About compliance again — do you provide SSO and RBAC integration? We need SAML and SCIM for user provisioning.
[06:22] Jamie: Yes, SAML and SCIM supported for Hosted with enterprise plan; Dedicated and Private have deeper integrations and role scoping per team.
[06:32] Priya: On SDKs — language support? We mostly use Python and Node but some services are Go.
[06:39] Samira: We have first-class Python and Node SDKs, beta Go SDK, and a REST API. The LangChain/LlamaIndex samples are Python focused but the REST adapter is easy to call from Go.
[06:51] Ravi: How painful is streaming in Go? Our agent loops expect partial responses.
[06:57] Samira: We expose server-sent events and HTTP chunked streaming; Go clients can handle this with standard libraries. We'll include a Go streaming snippet.
[07:10] Priya: Let's talk quotas again — if we set a per-tenant token cap, can we surface that to the tenant via headers so the frontend can show usage?
[07:20] Alex: Yes, you can opt into response headers that include remaining quota tokens and rate-limit reset windows. Also webhooks for usage thresholds.
[07:32] Maya: Observability — can we get model-level A/B dashboards? We want to run canaries.
[07:40] Jamie: You can create rollout policies for canary, A/B and automatic rollback if quality metrics drop. The console gives per-model dashboards and you can export metrics to your monitoring stack.
[07:52] [07:52] Speaker 1: nice
[07:56] Priya: A few practical questions — onboarding time for a sandbox and for Dedicated capacity?
[08:04] Alex: Sandbox hosted can be minutes — you get API keys and SDK. Dedicated capacity typically a few weeks depending on provisioning and contractual lead time; Private on-prem can be months for air-gapped installs.
[08:16] Carlos: If we start hosted, is migration to Private seamless? We want to migrate customers over time.
[08:23] Samira: Yes, that's one of our design goals — same API and SDK surface so swapping endpoints and pinning models is straightforward. We do have migration runbooks and testing steps.
[08:34] Ravi: Any known gotchas with LlamaIndex? We use a lot of custom retrievers and embeddings.
[08:41] Jamie: The main thing is embedding dimensionality and chunking semantics — we'll help align your ingestion pipeline and recommend embedding models and quant profiles. Also an eval harness to compare retrieval quality.
[08:55] Priya: Network security — do you support mTLS between our gateway and Redwood?
[09:01] Alex: Yes, mTLS is supported for private links and Dedicated connections. Hosted supports TLS and IP allowlists.
[09:10] Maya: Pricing — can you give a rough framing? Token cost vs reserved instances?
[09:17] Alex: We'll send a matrix. Short version: hosted is pay-as-you-go per token; Dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity model that reduces unit token cost and gives reserved throughput; Private is a combination of licensing and ops fee. We'll include example cost curves.
[09:34] [09:34] Priya: One more question on observability hooks — can we ship full request traces to our OTLP collector including prompt tokens?
[09:43] Jamie: We can ship traces and logs; prompt token content is sensitive so we provide redaction controls and a mode to only send token counts and embeddings hashes if you need PII minimization.
[09:55] Carlos: Good. That helps.
[09:58] Alex: Ok, to keep things concrete — Samira will drop SDK repos and LangChain/LlamaIndex examples. We'll run a cost/quality eval using your prompt suite. And Alex will send a Dedicated vs Private pricing + SLA doc.
[10:11] Priya: For the pilot, we expect 200 qps peak with 1-2k token average per request. Is that viable on Hosted pilot?
[10:23] Samira: You can pilot on Hosted but for sustained 200 qps with large tokens we'd recommend Dedicated to avoid noisy neighbor issues; for the pilot we can spin up a Dedicated reserved pool or a burst capacity plan.
[10:36] Ravi: Could you run a sample benchmark during the pilot to show latency percentiles and cost per 1k tokens?
[10:44] Alex: Yes, that's part of the pilot scope. We'll include p50/p90/p99 latency and cost curves.
[10:52] Maya: Let's schedule the benchmark session — tentatively 2 hours with infra and ML folks.
[10:59] [10:59] Action quick recap by Alex: pricing + SLAs, SDK repo, schedule benchmark, send SOC2 and KMS docs.
[11:10] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks.
[11:14] Carlos: Thank you — will consolidate compliance notes and send over.
[11:18] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with materials and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.
[11:24] End of call.
